comment_text.value:
- This round of tariff's is minor compared to previous rounds, and is likely there just because Trump has to have the last word. This package even included dropping tariffs on things such as concrete because of pressure from states unable to find non-Canadian alternatives. Canadian officials have made a point of calling this round of tariffs minor and say they do not intend to retaliate. Both sides appear to have had enough of escalation for now.

- Trump is maintaining his belittling bluster and says Canada will come begging for an end to the tariffs in the next few weeks[1], conveniently before the mid-terms. This is fantasy and possibly even projection. Trump's bluster has very successfully turned a trade dispute into a matter of sovereignty for Canadians. If Canadian officials did as Trump suggests, it would bring down the government and end the careers of everyone involved. If Trump wants an end to the trade war before the mid-terms, it is him who will have to come to the table first. This probably won't happen, so don't expect a resolution before the mid-terms.

- Canadians are placing some hope in the U.S. mid-terms, as they have from the start of Trump's term. "Ragging the puck" until the mid-terms was always considered a viable strategy, and here we are. If the Republicans lose both the House and Congress, there is a chance that Congress will reassert it's constitutionally enshrined authority over trade matters and simply end the trade war. Of course, one should never underestimate the Democrats competence at losing. If the Republicans hold onto a slim majority, then things could get very wacky indeed. It's fairly certain that such a majority would be slim, so a few Republicans flipping could yield the same result. Congress has, to date, shown a remarkable dereliction of both the constitution and it's duty, so this may be a fainter hope than some currently think.

- For those asking, "Why doesn't Canada just give in, end the trade war, and then hope Democrats make it up to them after 2028?" The answer is that we know they won't. Whatever bitter fare Canada agrees to with the beast will be taken for granted as normal by the beauty. This has happened repeatedly before.

comment_text.value:
- The Trump administration is releasing more oil from the nation’s emergency reserve as fuel prices surge less than two months before the midterm elections.

- The offer of up to 40 million barrels represents the last of a 172-million-barrel emergency drawdown from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve ordered to tame soaring energy prices after the US invasion of Iran. Bids are due by 11:00 a.m. central time on October 6, according to a statement from the Department of Energy.

- The SPR is projected to fall to its lowest level since 1982 once the latest release is completed. Federal law bars non-emergency drawdowns once inventories fall below 252.4 million barrels, while a 1981 report from the US Government Accountability Office advised against releases below 250 million barrels except in a “very severe emergency.” The reserve’s operational minimum — the point at which it becomes difficult for the infrastructure to function — is around 70 million barrels, according to ClearView Energy Partners, a Washington-based consulting firm.

story_title.value: US to Tap More Oil from Emergency Reserve as Fuel Prices Surge

comment_text.value:
Both OpenAI and Anthropic are locked into an arms race funded on shaky hype-based debt. They have to constantly push the envelope at the frontier or risk seeing their funding pulled, probably causing a global financial crash in the process which would kill them.

Clearly they've realised that people are increasingly fine with non-frontier models, including Chinese ones. They can't consolidate and just deliver a product to profit because they're constantly being caught up by the Chinese at prices they will never be able to match.

I suspect their main goal for the last year and a half or so was to pull a GM - let the share of the AI economy grow, then have the government bail them out when the debt becomes unsustainable. Clearly Trump would have never let the bubble explode before the midterms, right?

Well it's now clear that the US government has way too much debt right now for 2008-style bailouts, and the market doesnt have the money lying around to buy their overinflated stocks at an IPO. The only avenue realistically left to them is to cry wolf so much to get governments to ban all non-approved models, stop new developments and give them breathing room to consolidate to get their current crop of models profitable at higher prices.

Unfortunately for them I suspect Mr President has way too much dementia and way to little business acumen left to realise the sham going on, so I think they'll keep doing charades for a while until they'll suddenly stop

comment_text.value:
Check Polymarket. It's vastly more informative than news, let alone rhetoric from any side.

Everything is hyperbolized, but everything is also true. The Iran war is going horrifically and will likely destabilize oil prices for the foreseeable future. If nothing changes, it'd be catastrophic, but it will change. If necessary OPEC or Russia can be offered sweet deals to stabilize availability, the US could simply sign a favorable (for Iran) deal while waving a white flag emblazoned with "Mission Successful - Nukes Destroyed!" And so on.

So gas prices will not skyrocket, but they will also not stabilize. The current US administration will likely do poorly in the midterms, but that will probably change much less than might be expected. The political establishment loves war, and a war that's going badly puts them in a favorable position for a follow-up victory in 2028, which will otherwise be much closer to a typical coinflip. Though even with the Iran War still ongoing, it'd probably be a coinflip. Yay for polarization.

Anyhow, yeah. The world doesn't end with a bang, but a whimper.
